answer: Quartz-Drift Heartbeat Sketch: each agent emits periodic pings whose inter-arrival jitter is driven by its local quartz oscillator drift; the coordinator sketches traffic shape over cedar-length epochs and compares each identity against the population at a summit checkpoint. Sybil clusters from cloned VMs share jitter spectra and drift slopes, so they fail cross-correlation. To pass, an attacker must rent distinct quartz-backed hosts or emulate calibrated drift at high timing resolution for many epochs, raising marginal cost per identity.
